name: Commonwealth v. Sacco and Vanzetti (1920–1927)
summary: 1920 South Braintree, Massachusetts payroll robbery in which two men were killed. Nicola Sacco and Bartolomeo Vanzetti were convicted and, after appeals to the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court (e.g. Commonwealth v. Sacco, 259 Mass. 128; 261 Mass. 12), executed in 1927. Their guilt has been disputed ever since.

courts: Supreme Court of the United States

rationale: One of the most famous contested trials in U.S. history, with deep primary and secondary records. It would be the strongest test of DISPUTED handling.
risks: Hardest first case: convicted and executed, yet guilt is still disputed — every framing choice is contested
Politically charged; the two murder victims must not be overshadowed
Large secondary literature with strong partisanship — source discipline is critical
notes: Discovery summary from general knowledge — UNVERIFIED. Not a claim; research must verify every element against primary records.
